label: L=9 copy start (first copy-input step), boosted when echoed first token is z/n/l
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate neuron, active only in the copy phase of length-9 sequences: about 82% of activations (and mass) at t=10 (recall_idx=1, input = echoed first original token, right after <DEL>) and the rest at t=11 (recall_idx=2); 3 activations in L=8 and none in the original or delimiter phase or for L<=7. Even inside that context it fires on only about 2% of steps (L==9 & recall_idx in {1,2} gives recall 0.99 but precision 0.01). What decides firing within the context is mainly the identity of the echoed first token: z (12x lift, the largest activations, e.g. a z z z ... start), then n and l, with 1/b/2 weaker. Restricting to those tokens raises precision to about 0.15 but drops recall to about 0.6. I checked the last original token (orig(8)) as a further condition and it did not help. Most z/n/l starts at L=9 still do not fire, so the description is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues.
